title: Superconductors and the Maglev System
sourceLabel: 既存教材をTOEFL形式へ変換 · 元の問1–9に対応
verificationNote: 原文と全九つの学習対象を保持し、日本語記述・翻訳・発展問題を本文根拠のある英語四択へ変換しました。

passages.text:
A superconductor is not merely a very good ordinary conductor. Below a material-dependent critical temperature, it can carry direct current with zero electrical resistance under appropriate conditions. When a material enters the superconducting state, it also exhibits the Meissner effect: magnetic flux is expelled from its interior, apart from the more complicated behaviour of practical type-II materials. Zero resistance and magnetic-field response are related features of the same quantum state, but they answer different experimental questions.

The phrase “zero resistance” is powerful and easy to overextend. A useful device must remain within limits of temperature, magnetic field, and current density. Cooling requires equipment and energy. Alternating fields and changing currents can introduce losses in a real system even when steady direct-current resistance is zero. Superconductivity therefore removes a particular electrical loss under defined conditions; it does not remove every energy cost from a machine.

This distinction matters when explaining a superconducting magnetic-levitation railway. In the Japanese SCMaglev design, superconducting magnets are carried on the vehicle. Coils installed along the guideway serve different functions. Propulsion coils create a moving magnetic pattern that pulls and pushes the train forward. As the vehicle moves at sufficient speed, its magnetic field induces currents in levitation and guidance coils. The resulting electromagnetic forces lift the vehicle and keep it centred. The train initially uses wheels and rises only after reaching the required speed.

A classroom demonstration of a magnet floating above a cooled superconductor can reveal important physics, but it is not a complete scale model of that railway. The demonstration foregrounds flux expulsion and, in type-II materials, flux pinning. The transport system depends on onboard magnets, guideway geometry, controlled switching, electromagnetic induction, cryogenic engineering, vehicle dynamics, and safety systems. Good explanation moves between levels: quantum state, material, magnet, coil, vehicle, and infrastructure. It states which level supplies each part of the causal chain.

questions.prompt: What is the main purpose of the passage?

options.label: A
options.text: To claim a floating magnet alone constitutes a complete railway.

options.label: B
options.text: To show cooling and drag have no cost.

options.label: C
options.text: To distinguish superconducting properties and explain how multiple railway subsystems use them.

options.label: D
options.text: To argue that trains levitate while standing still in every design.

questions.answer: 正解：C。超伝導の性質と磁気浮上鉄道の推進・浮上・案内・冷却を区別して結びます。

questions.prompt: How are zero DC resistance and the Meissner effect different?

options.label: A
options.text: The first concerns DC electrical resistance; the second concerns the magnetic-field response of a superconductor.

options.label: B
options.text: Both mean that all alternating-current losses disappear.

options.label: C
options.text: The first concerns magnetic pinning; the second concerns ticket prices.

options.label: D
options.text: Both are names for aerodynamic lift from wings.

questions.answer: 正解：A。第1段落。電気抵抗と磁束排除という別の性質です。

questions.prompt: Which three limits can end a superconducting state?

options.label: A
options.text: Ticket price, train length, and station spacing.

options.label: B
options.text: Humidity, rail color, and passenger weight only.

options.label: C
options.text: Temperature, wheel diameter, and timetable precision.

options.label: D
options.text: Temperature, magnetic field, and current density exceeding their critical values.

questions.answer: 正解：D。第1段落の温度・磁場・電流密度の臨界条件です。

questions.prompt: Why does zero DC resistance not imply zero energy cost for a maglev railway?

options.label: A
options.text: Because the onboard magnets are always ordinary permanent magnets.

options.label: B
options.text: Cooling, alternating-current losses, propulsion, and aerodynamic drag still require energy.

options.label: C
options.text: Because zero resistance means no current can flow.

options.label: D
options.text: Because levitation abolishes every form of electrical power use.

questions.answer: 正解：B。第2段落。材料の直流抵抗ゼロと鉄道全体のエネルギー収支は異なります。

questions.prompt: Which roles do the guideway systems have?

options.label: A
options.text: The propulsion coils only cool the passenger cabin.

options.label: B
options.text: All coils merely prevent the onboard magnet from conducting.

options.label: C
options.text: A moving magnetic pattern propels the train, while induced currents in levitation and guidance coils help lift and center it.

options.label: D
options.text: Levitation coils replace all motors, braking, and control.

questions.answer: 正解：C。第3段落。推進用の進行磁界と浮上・案内用の誘導電流を分けます。

questions.prompt: Why does the described SCMaglev initially run on wheels?

options.label: A
options.text: Its magnets have not been manufactured yet.

options.label: B
options.text: Induced lift needs sufficient movement, so wheels support it at low speed.

options.label: C
options.text: It cannot carry superconducting magnets while stopped.

options.label: D
options.text: The passage says the guideway has no coils.

questions.answer: 正解：B。低速では誘導による十分な浮上力が得られないため、初めは車輪を使います。

options.label: A
options.text: The onboard magnetic field induces current in the guideway levitation/guidance coils, and their interaction supplies lift and centering.

options.label: B
options.text: Only gravity and the wheel bearings.

options.label: C
options.text: An aircraft wing moving through air.

options.label: D
options.text: A passenger’s phone attracting the rails.

questions.answer: 正解：A。指示語は車上磁石と地上コイルの誘導・相互作用を受けます。

questions.prompt: What does “A material property is not yet a railway” emphasize?

options.label: A
options.text: Material science is irrelevant to vehicles.

options.label: B
options.text: A classroom levitation demonstration includes every safety and control system.

options.label: C
options.text: Cooling is unnecessary once a magnet floats.

options.label: D
options.text: A full railway also needs magnets, coils, propulsion, control, cooling, vehicle design, and safety integration.

questions.answer: 正解：D。最終段落。物性実験と社会実装された交通システムの階層差です。

questions.prompt: Which analogy best applies the passage’s demonstration-versus-system distinction?

options.label: A
options.text: A glowing solar cell under a lamp proves all power plants need no grid.

options.label: B
options.text: An individual device always guarantees identical performance at city scale.

options.label: C
options.text: A solar cell under a lamp demonstrates conversion, while a reliable power system also needs wiring, inverters, weather planning, and maintenance.

options.label: D
options.text: A magnet floating in a classroom means energy and control costs are zero.

questions.answer: 正解：C。発展問題。単体の原理実証と周辺設備・変動・保守を含む運用を区別します。
